name: Ironveil Quickpeel Extraction Operative Rig
description: This is the outfit of someone who expects to need a second identity before the night is over. The outer layer is a structured jacket in deep forest green with a brushed matte finish — it reads as Tier 3 business-casual at a distance, the kind of thing a mid-management logistics coordinator might wear to a site visit. The jacket's inner face is a reversed charcoal-black with minimal texture, transforming the silhouette entirely when flipped; the collar reconfigures via a hidden snap system to shift from a spread collar to a standing Mandarin style, completing the look change. Integrated along both inner breast panels are dual holster channels with polymer retention clips, and a series of six micro-pockets sized for comm gear, breach tools, and injection cartridges run along the inner hem. The shirt beneath is a deep burgundy fitted button-down in scanner-resistant silk-synthetic blend, worn tucked into straight-cut trousers in charcoal with aug-compatible side-seam channels — the left seam runs a full power-routing strip from hip to ankle for chrome-leg users, with an external port at the boot cuff. Boots are clean-line Chelsea-style in dark brown synthetic leather with a hidden blade channel in the right shaft. A slim wrist-wrap on the left forearm houses a passive comm relay and a micro-display strip readable only at close angle.
functionality: Reversible jacket with collar reconfiguration system, dual integrated holster channels, six hem micro-pockets, full-length aug-power routing left trouser seam, hidden boot-shaft blade channel, passive comm relay wrist wrap
what_it_says: This rig says its wearer has money and experience in roughly equal measure. The Tier 3-4 surface read opens doors that a Shelf-coded outfit never would, while the hidden architecture underneath speaks to someone who has been in enough situations to build redundancy into every layer. Runners who recognize the collar snap system know immediately who they're dealing with.
worn_by: social-engineering operatives who work corporate floors
manufacturer: Duskframe Collective — a mid-tier street label known for garments that pass corporate dress codes while concealing serious tactical infrastructure
story_hooks: The runner makes it through a Tier 4 corporate checkpoint on the jacket's business-casual read, but the passive comm relay in the wrist wrap begins broadcasting on a frequency the building's security system is actively hunting — the runner has maybe four minutes before triangulation.

A contact uses the collar snap configuration as a recognition signal — standing collar means the meeting is clean, spread collar means they're being watched — and the runner arrives with the wrong configuration because of a hasty reversal in a stairwell.

The blade channel in the boot shaft sets off a legacy mag-sensor at a private venue entrance, the kind of scanner that shouldn't be picking up composite materials — someone upgraded the security without telling the fixer who arranged the job.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively corporate silhouette that conceals tactical infrastructure. Forest green structured jacket reads as mid-management logistics wear at distance, but reverses to charcoal-black for rapid identity shift. Worn over fitted burgundy button-down and straight-cut charcoal trousers. Clean, professional lines that mask extensive gear integration.
physical_description.fit: Tailored and structured through the torso; jacket sits sharp at shoulders with room for holster channels beneath. Shirt fitted but not restrictive; trousers straight-cut with deliberate seam architecture. Overall impression: controlled, ready, deceptively casual.
physical_description.primary_material: Outer jacket: brushed matte synthetic (reversible). Shirt: scanner-resistant silk-synthetic blend. Trousers: charcoal synthetic twill with integrated power-routing strip. Boots: dark brown synthetic leather.
physical_description.texture: Jacket outer: matte, non-reflective. Jacket inner: smooth charcoal. Shirt: subtle weave, slight grip texture. Trousers: flat twill with seam detailing. Boots: polished but scuffed from use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: forest green (outer) / charcoal black (inner reverse). Accent: deep burgundy (shirt), dark brown (boots). Muted, low-visibility palette.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: hidden snap system for collar reconfiguration, primary zip likely concealed. Shirt: standard button-down. Trousers: friction-fit waistband with discreet augmentation access ports. Boots: side zip with blade channel retention.
distinctive_features: Reversible jacket design for rapid identity shift
Dual holster channels with polymer retention clips on inner breast panels
Six micro-pockets along inner hem for comm gear and breach tools
Full power-routing strip along left trouser seam (aug-compatible, hip to ankle)
External power port at boot cuff for chrome-leg compatibility

physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional with Tier 2 tactical infrastructure. Reads corporate-legitimate at surface level; actual purpose signals operator-class street professional.
physical_description.cultural_context: Extraction operative, intelligence contractor, or corpo black-ops field agent. Someone who needs plausible deniability and rapid tactical repositioning. The 'second identity before nightfall' aesthetic speaks to high-stakes work in GLMZ ungoverned zones.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine outer presentation; inner infrastructure shows minimal wear from professional maintenance. Boots subtly scuffed from field use but kept operationally clean. No visible patching—this is maintained gear, not salvage.
